newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse tells investors to use discretion.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse tells investors to use discretion.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand on Monday issued a statement urging equity investors not to panic and to be cautious in their analysis and response to the on-going turmoil in the finance sector.

"The SET would like to advise the shareholders of all the bank and finance companies involved, as well as other investors to exercise caution in analysing the present situation," the exchange said in a statement.
The release came after the central bank's closure of 16 financially troubled finance companies on Friday. Nine of those firms are listed and trading in their shares is currently halted.
The government has pledged to protect creditors and depositors from the fallout of the move which is designed to bolster stability in the ailing industry.

"The SET recommends all parties use their discretion in assessing any news connected to these developments and not to panic or overreact to any sensational headlines or news reports presented by the media or independent investment analysts," the exchange said.

The Bank of Thailand said early on Monday there would be no announcements of more new troubled finance firms. Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond also urged investors not to panic and said authorities would do their best to help depositors of the foreign creditors of troubled finance companies recover their funds.

The Thai finance and securities sector is struggling to cope with declining revenues, high funding costs and a deterioration in asset quality as Thailand goes through its worst economic downturn for more than a decade.
The Thai bourse has tumbled 36.5 percent so far this year and the stock index is lingering round eight year lows. The market was up 1.16 percent after 50 minutes of trade at 534.33 points on Monday.
